solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pam rang excitedly — "This includes every letter!"

indicators.note: acting excitedly, the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Pam phones in a state, announcing she has found something that contains the whole alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pam rang' looks like a woman making a call; 'excitedly' tells you to rearrange its seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pangram is a sentence using all twenty-six letters of the alphabet at least once.

clue.text: Dull walker

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means plodding and uninspired

explanation.surface: A boring person who goes about on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lacking imagination; the noun means a person on foot rather than in a vehicle.

clue.text: Relative, friendly, full of energy

indicators.note: the word for friendly is filled with the energy letter, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A family member who is pleasant and lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relation.

clue.text: On the rise again, urges rent changes

indicators.note: the letters of the two words undergo changes, giving a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something reviving prompts a landlord to alter the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something rising or reviving after a decline.

clue.text: Way big house is spoken of

indicators.note: the word for a big house is spoken, and what is heard gives the answer's sound

parts.note: a manor is a large country house

explanation.surface: Describing the style in which a mansion is talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner and way are synonyms for the method or style in which something is done.

clue.text: Girl with zeal's first to give canal name

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word zeal

explanation.surface: A keen young woman lends her name to a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suez Canal in Egypt links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.

clue.text: Caught sight of cutting tool

definitions.meaning: a toothed blade for cutting wood

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the past tense of see; the other is the toothed blade used by carpenters.

clue.text: Short piece expert distributed round start of class

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the single letter, enclosing it
the letters of the word expert are distributed into a new order
start of takes only the opening letter of the word class

explanation.surface: A specialist hands out a brief passage at the beginning of a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' makes EXERPT from EXPERT; 'round' puts it around C, the start of 'class'.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract taken from a longer text or piece of music.

clue.text: Fitting of French to protect university

indicators.note: the French word surrounds the university letter as if guarding it

explanation.surface: Something French made to shield a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Due means appropriate or proper, as in due respect, the same sense as fitting.

clue.text: Cinque Port snack maybe

definitions.meaning: ... in Kent is one of the Cinque Ports

explanation.surface: A south-coast harbour town that might also be a light bite.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports are a historic group of English Channel towns in Kent and Sussex; Sandwich is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwich is both the Kent town and the filled bread named after the Earl of Sandwich.

clue.text: Drinks for all before a fight — devious!

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for everyone in the group
a bout is a boxing match or fight

explanation.surface: A pub scene where drinks for everyone precede a brawl, all rather underhand.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying a round means paying for drinks for the whole group, a British pub custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundabout as an adjective means indirect or circuitous, a mild sense of devious.

clue.text: Argue about English weapon

indicators.note: the word for argue sits about the English letter, surrounding it

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute

explanation.surface: Disputing over an English armament.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long-shafted thrusting or throwing weapon.

clue.text: Ban eastern doctor associated with Jason's ship

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: An oriental physician linked to the Argonauts' vessel is prohibited.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade, so it is a kind of ban.

clue.text: Bless male after conversion that's clear

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are converted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A blessing given to a man after he converts to a faith shows he is free of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Blameless means free from guilt, as when someone is cleared of fault.

clue.text: Dishonest scheme — uproar!

explanation.surface: A swindle that causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Racket covers both a fraudulent business and a loud, disturbing noise.

clue.text: 100 as old as us showing mettle

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
something as old as us is of our age

explanation.surface: A centenarian of our generation displaying spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle means spirit or bravery in the face of difficulty, which is courage.

clue.text: Fan crossing street, European, for tie

indicators.note: the fan word spans the other letters, holding them inside it

explanation.surface: A supporter walking across the road with a continental neckwear item.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten and to tie are synonyms for securing something.

clue.text: Uncommon sign of injury — Anglicans providing support

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits beneath the first, holding it up

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a wound
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A rare wound mark, with the Church of England offering help.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means in short supply, so rarely found.

clue.text: Referring to centres for swimming, a CA quit, upset

indicators.note: the letters of these words are upset and tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A chartered accountant resigns in a huff over swimming pools.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is a chartered accountant; here its letters are simply part of the jumbled material.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquatic centres are swimming pool complexes, so the adjective is what such centres are called.

clue.text: Run more

definitions.meaning: in cricket an ... is a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide

explanation.surface: A command to keep running further.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs credited to the batting side from bowling errors rather than hits.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a cricket run from a wide or no-ball; as an adjective it means additional.

clue.text: Right designation

definitions.meaning: a legal right to own property

explanation.surface: The correct label for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Title means a legal claim to ownership and also a name such as Lord or Dr.

clue.text: Some logjam, bore, ending — there's celebration!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tedious traffic jam finally ends and everyone parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large festive gathering, so a party or celebration.

clue.text: Horse betting attracts you first of all

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Gambling on a racehorse lures you in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a horse with a reddish-brown coat and black points.

clue.text: At Sodom regularly? Excessively!

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A question about frequent visits to the biblical city of sin, answered with disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Too as an adverb means more than is acceptable, so excessively.

clue.text: Levity? Forget it — this must be paid

indicators.note: forget tells you to leave out the word it from the longer word

explanation.surface: Stop joking; this charge is serious and has to be settled.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a tax or charge imposed by authority, something owed.

clue.text: After redevelopment, sea site most comfortable

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are redeveloped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A seafront plot, once rebuilt, is the cosiest place to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiest is the superlative of easy, which can mean relaxed and comfortable.
